summary.title: COVID-19: Face Mask Detector with OpenCV, Keras/TensorFlow, and Deep Learning
summary.one_liner: You learn how to train a MobileNetV2-based face mask classifier on a custom dataset with Keras/TensorFlow and then run it on static images and webcam video using OpenCV face detection.
keywords: embedded computer vision raspberry pi mask detection
takeaways: Train a face mask classifier by fine-tuning MobileNetV2 with ImageNet weights, a new FC head, and frozen base layers.
Load and preprocess a 1,376-image dataset (with_mask / without_mask) and use ImageDataGenerator augmentation with an 80/20 split.
Use a separate OpenCV face detector to locate faces, then classify each face as with_mask or without_mask in static images and webcam streams.
Create artificial mask training data by placing a transparent mask on faces using facial landmarks, but keep non-mask images separate from source images to avoid bias.
summary.summary: The post builds a two-phase COVID-19 face mask detector: a training script that fine-tunes MobileNetV2 in Keras/TensorFlow on a dataset of 1,376 images, and deployment scripts that use OpenCV face detection plus the trained classifier on static images and webcam video. It explains how the dataset was made by applying masks to face photos with facial landmarks, and warns against reusing source images as non-mask examples. The author reports about 99% test accuracy after 20 epochs, with the training run shown in the post. The page text is cut off partway through the image-detection script's argument parsing.
